---
name: elevenlabs
description: >-
  Turn a Markdown script into per-paragraph AI narration with the `elevenlabs` CLI
  (grdev.elevenlabs-cli) — one MP3 per paragraph, cached by content so editing one paragraph
  never re-pays for the rest. Use whenever the user wants a script voiced or a voice track
  produced, including phrasings like "narrate this script", "generate voiceover", "make the
  audio for this video script", "read this out with ElevenLabs", "re-render the paragraph I
  changed", or "how much will narrating this cost". Also use when an `elevenlabs` run has
  failed and the message needs interpreting — a missing `voiceId`, a missing or rejected API
  key, or exhausted credits. Covers the script frontmatter, the content-addressed cache, the
  `--dry-run` cost preview, `--watch`, and the one step a human has to do.
---

# Narrating a Markdown script

The `elevenlabs` CLI is built to be driven by an agent: nothing prompts, and the exit code says
what happened. It calls a **paid** API — every cache miss spends ElevenLabs credits, charged per
character — so `--dry-run` comes first, every time.

## Check the tool is there

```bash
elevenlabs version
```

Not found → `dotnet tool install --global grdev.elevenlabs-cli`.

## The two layers

Understanding these is what makes the tool safe to re-run:

| Layer | Path | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Cache** | `<output>/.cache` | The expensive, immutable asset. One `<hash>.mp3` per distinct paragraph-plus-voice, keyed by content only |
| **Output** | `<output>/` | A cheap, disposable projection — `NN - first five words.mp3`, rebuilt from the cache on every run |

The hash covers the normalized paragraph text and the voice settings, and deliberately **not**
the paragraph's position. That is what lets you reorder paragraphs, split one into two, or
insert a new one and pay only for what genuinely changed. Every other clip is a free copy out
of the cache.

Each run also **deletes any `.mp3` in the output folder it did not pr
[truncated]
